title: Mohr's Circle Visualiser
scope: 3D stress and small-strain transformation for an isotropic linear-elastic material: principal values and directions (Jacobi), three Mohr circles with the admissible region, 2D circles as rotations about x, y, z or a principal axis, plane stress and plane strain, Hooke's law, Tresca, Mohr–Coulomb, Rankine and von Mises checks, and a strain-gauge rosette helper.
conventions: Internally stress is in MPa and tension positive; strain is dimensionless with tensor shear ε_xy = γ_xy/2. Display, input and export convert.
Compression positive negates the whole displayed tensor (σ' = −σ), so σ1 is the largest value in that convention and compression runs to the right.
2D shear convention A plots tensor-positive τ downward: a counter-clockwise element rotation θ moves the point counter-clockwise by 2θ. Convention B plots τ upward and the point moves clockwise.
The 3D view plots the resolved shear magnitude τ ≥ 0; strain circles plot ε against γ/2.
Factors of safety use proportional load scaling: the factor k on every stress component that brings the state to the criterion. ∞ means no failure under proportional loading.
The von Mises line on the Mohr plane is a reference at τ = σy/√3 (pure-shear yield), not a true envelope.
